title: Annotatio II §.IX (4): Body corporally in one place — heaven now; Vigilius; Luther’s Bible preface
pass_a_gloss: (4) By the nature of Christ’s Body, which is corporally in one place only, and as at the time of the instituted Supper it was corporally at the table, not however at once above the table in the bread, or in Christ’s hands taking and breaking the bread; So at the time of the Supper still celebrated and to be celebrated, it is corporally in the heavens and remains in the heavens, the Holy Spirit witnessing (Acts 3:21) and Christ Himself, even in the Institution words (Matt. 26:29; 1 Cor. 11:26). And just as Christ’s flesh, while it was corporally on earth, was by no means in Heaven; so now because it is corporally in the heavens, it is by no means on earth, says Blessed Vigilius bk. 4. Hence Luther himself, in the last words of his preface to the Bible, writes thus: The High Priest’s sons who deal with the daily sacrifice should point to us Christians, who before our Father Christ sitting in Heaven dwell here on earth with the body, and are not yet through with Him except spiritually by faith. Where observe Luther saying three things: (1) Christ sits in Heaven, we are bodily on earth. (2) We are not bodily with Christ. (3) We are with Christ no otherwise than spiritually and by faith.
pass_b_english: (4) Christ’s body is corporally in one place only — at the Institution at the table, not also in the bread in His hands; now corporally in heaven (Acts 3:21; Matt. 26:29; 1 Cor. 11:26).
Vigilius: as when on earth it was not in heaven, so now in heaven it is not on earth.
Luther’s Bible preface: we dwell on earth with the body before Christ seated in heaven, and are with Him only spiritually by faith — three points Strimesius marks.
source_text: (4) Naturæ Corporis Christi, quod corporaliter in uno tantum loco est, & uti tempore institutæ Coenæ, ad mensam corporaliter, non autem simul supra mensam, in pane, vel in manibus Christi panem sumentibus & frangentibus, fuit; Ita tempore celebratæ adhuc & celebrandæ Coenæ, corporaliter in cælis est & in cælis manet teste Spir. S. Act. 3, 21. ipsôque Christô, etiam in Institutionis Coenæ verbis Matth. 26, 29. 1. Cor. 11, 26. Quemadmodum verò caro Christi, dum in terra fuit corporaliter, non utique erat in Cœlo; ita nunc quia in cælis est corporaliter, non est utique in terris, ait B. Vigilius Lib. 4. Hinc Lutherus ipse, postremis verbis præfationis suæ in Biblia, sic scribit: Des Hohen Priesters Söhne / Die mit dem täglichen Opfer umgehen / sollten auff uns Christen deuten / die wir für unserm Vater Christo / im Himmel sitzend / hie auff Erden / mit dem Leibe wohnen / und nicht hin Durch sind bey ihm / ohne mit dem Glauben geistlich. Ubi observa Lutherum tria dicere (1) Christum sedere in Cœlo, nos corpore esse in terra. (2) Nos corpore non esse cum Christo. (3) Non aliter, quam spiritualiter & per fidem, nos esse cum Christo.

choices.english: was by no means in Heaven

notes: (4) One place; heaven; Vigilius; Luther preface.
